question: Can a separately authored, statically linked provider contribute one specialized Metal physical implementation alongside the governed provider without forking or replacing tiler-metal?
answer: No, at the commit recorded below. Two independent blockers, both in tiler-compiler; neither is in tiler-metal, which needs no change at all.

gates: COST_MODEL_KEY = "tiler.cost.structural.v1" (frontier.rs:80) — a private const with no public spelling; any other key is a hard FrontierError::MalformedCostProvenance
region::SemanticMemberId (region.rs:123) — what FrontierRegionSubject is made of
physical::{pointwise_region, reduction_region, fused_region} (physical.rs:227, 309, 397) — how the governed provider builds a body
pipeline::compile (pipeline.rs:580) — the internal path that supplies the provider array
blocking_private_surfaces.not_blocking: request::{TargetProfile, TargetProfileKey} are pub(crate) re-exports (request.rs:34) of public tiler_compiler::target types, so they are reachable.

blocking_private_surfaces.statement: Independent of visibility. The provider array is a hardcoded one-element literal at crates/tiler-compiler/src/pipeline/planning.rs:171, and the internal CompilationRequest (request.rs:542) carries no provider field, so making the frontier public would still leave a provider uninstallable. This is exactly the asymmetry ADR 0078 item 4 named and closed for lowering providers, still open for physical ones.

Populated from the lowering capability registry (session.rs:1443). The governed physical provider's identity, tiler/prototype-serial-sum-physical, does not appear in it, and neither PlanAlternative nor Compilation exposes physical-provider provenance. A third party can neither register a physical provider nor observe that it failed to.

claims.statement: An out-of-workspace crate reaches the real compile path through tiler_compiler::session::compile_governed and receives a selected plan.

The body a proposal wraps is a tiler_ir::schedule::ScheduledRegion, fully constructible from outside the workspace. The blocked seam is registration and re-verification, not the expression of an implementation.

threads_per_workgroup is free under the intrinsic verifier (tiler-ir/src/schedule/builder.rs:288) and is folded into CanonicalScheduledRegionIdentity (tiler-ir/src/schedule/model.rs:892). A 32-thread workgroup and the governed 1-thread workgroup over the same index region are therefore additive alternatives with distinct identities, not one implementation twice.

verify_region_subject_binding (physical.rs:700) compares region id, iteration shape, scalar program, semantic members, and access map against the compiler's own normalized expectation, and says nothing about KernelSchedule. So the binding constrains what a region means and not how it is scheduled — a specialized provider is semantically expressible under the existing gate.
claims.boundary: The binding itself is private and unreachable from the spike; this claim is read from the source, not exercised.

claims.statement: The provider crate does not depend on tiler-metal. The probe lowers its region with tiler_ir::kernel::lower_scheduled_region and emits with tiler_metal::emit::emit_translation_unit, both public, and the flushing realization it declares passes require_declared_realization on the Apple facts. No interface prevents a custom physical provider from reusing standard Metal emission.

The two alternatives emit byte-identical kernel bodies under distinct entry-point symbols, because the symbol is derived from an identity the workgroup width participates in. Launch geometry is carried by the dispatch, not by the emitted statements.
claims.outcome: distinct symbols, identical bodies modulo identity digests

claims.statement: A body whose launch.grid_threads is one short of the iteration domain is rejected by ScheduledRegionBuilder::build with exactly [LaunchCoverage] (rule "launch-coverage"). That is the same call the frontier makes on a provider's body (physical.rs:652) and the diagnostic it maps onto PhysicalError::Intrinsic (physical.rs:684).

unreachable_from_this_spike.reason: Requires two providers in one enumerate_frontier call. The trait, the function, and the provider array are all private, and the public boundary discloses no physical provider.
unreachable_from_this_spike.existing_in_crate_evidence: crates/tiler-compiler/src/frontier.rs:2511-2512 enumerates the same two providers forward and reversed and compares the result; that is an in-crate unit test, not evidence a cross-crate provider can participate.

unreachable_from_this_spike.reason: Contention is a property of the lowering capability registry, which is a different seam from the physical frontier. Frontier alternatives are additive by construction and have no contention to demonstrate. Conflating the two is what the ticket's own graph-maintenance section forbids.

Enforced by construction: ImplementationProposal carries only a body, an applicability predicate, and a cost (frontier.rs:726), and the frontier stamps provenance and derives resources and the boundary contract itself. Read from source; not exercisable without the private trait.

assess_region and the request/realization equality check either side of the subject binding are private (physical.rs:655, 659). The spike exercises the intrinsic verifier between them and nothing else.

falsification_runs.procedure: Copy the spike outside the repository, rewrite the three tiler-* path dependencies to absolute paths, replace .with_physical_providers(..) in the fail fixture with .with_capabilities(InstalledCapabilities::governed()), and rerun.
falsification_runs.observed: test tests/ui/fail/no_physical_provider_installation_seam.rs [should fail to compile] ... error / Expected test case to fail to compile, but it succeeded.

falsification_runs.procedure: In the same copy, replace `use tiler_compiler::region::SemanticMemberId;` with an import of the public `tiler_compiler::capability::LoweringFamily`, and rerun.
falsification_runs.observed: test tests/ui/fail/provider_inputs_are_private.rs [should fail to compile] ... mismatch — the region E0603 disappeared from the actual output and the byte comparison went red.

measurement_boundary: Facts about one compiler, one host, and one commit. The .stderr goldens are the rendering of a diagnostic, not a stability guarantee: a later rustc may reword E0603 or E0599 without any change to Tiler. A red trybuild run means the question has been reopened and must be re-answered, never that a golden should be blessed to make it green. Nothing here measures runtime behaviour, cost-model comparability across providers, or what a second provider would do to selection.
